meaning: First finger next to the thumb; on most grips it sits on or across a seam and can lead pressure.
example_en: Put a little more pressure on your index finger.
example_es: Ponle un poquito más de presión al dedo índice.

meaning: Longest finger; leads pressure on many sliders, curveballs and cutters.
example_en: Keep your middle finger right on the seam.
example_es: Mantén el dedo del medio encima de la costura.
region_note: MLB.com en español writes 'dedo medio'; 'dedo del medio' is the everyday form (unverified in print).

meaning: Fourth finger; usually rests on the side of the ball, and helps carry a circle changeup.
example_en: Your ring finger is too far under the ball.
example_es: Tienes el anular muy abajo de la pelota.

meaning: Smallest finger; on most grips it rests off the ball or against the side.
example_en: Tuck your pinky against the side of the ball.
example_es: Pega el meñique al lado de la pelota.
region_note: 'Dedo chiquito' is informal; verify how common it is with Dominican players.

meaning: Supports the ball from underneath or the side; its position changes how deep the ball sits and how it comes out.
example_en: Move your thumb a little more under the ball.
example_es: Mueve el pulgar un poquito más abajo de la pelota.
region_note: 'Dedo gordo' is common colloquial Caribbean usage for the thumb (and big toe); 'pulgar' is understood everywhere.

meaning: Pads at the end of the fingers; holding the ball 'on the fingertips' means less palm contact.
example_en: Hold it more on your fingertips.
example_es: Agárrala más con la punta de los dedos.
region_note: 'La punta de los dedos' is the more natural field phrase; 'yemas' is more precise.

meaning: Finger joint; relevant for knuckle-curve grips where a fingertip is tucked.
example_en: Tuck the index finger so the knuckle points at the catcher.
example_es: Dobla el índice para que el nudillo apunte al cátcher.

meaning: Joint between hand and forearm; wrist position at release (behind, on top of, or to the side of the ball) shapes spin.
example_en: Keep your wrist behind the ball.
example_es: Mantén la muñeca detrás de la pelota.

meaning: Inside of the hand; how much the ball touches the palm is part of grip depth.
example_en: Don't let the ball touch your palm on the fastball.
example_es: Que la pelota no te toque la palma en la recta.

meaning: The ball itself.
example_en: Show me how you hold the ball.
example_es: Enséñame cómo agarras la pelota.
region_note: 'Bola' also means 'ball' in the count; use 'pelota' for the object to avoid confusion. 'Pelota' also names the sport in the DR ('la pelota').

meaning: The raised red stitching; finger placement and seam orientation are described relative to them.
example_en: Find the seams with your fingers.
example_es: Busca las costuras con los dedos.

meaning: The wide U-shaped seam pattern used as the reference for the four-seam grip.
example_en: Put your fingers across the horseshoe.
example_es: Pon los dedos atravesados sobre la herradura.

meaning: How the ball is turned in the hand, which determines which seams lead in flight and can create seam-shifted wake effects.
example_en: Let's turn the ball a little so the seams are different.
example_es: Vamos a girar un poco la pelota para cambiar las costuras.

meaning: How the pitcher holds the ball: finger placement, pressure and depth.
example_en: Let's try a slightly deeper grip.
example_es: Vamos a probar un agarre un poquito más profundo.
region_note: 'Agarre' confirmed in MLB.com en español ('ajustar el agarre', 'un agarre firme'). 'Grip' as a loanword is heard but unverified as dominant.

meaning: To hold the ball in a grip.
example_en: Grip it like your fastball.
example_es: Agárrala como tu recta.
region_note: 'Coger' is normal in the DR and Caribbean; avoid it with Mexican or Argentine players, where it is vulgar.

meaning: Index and middle fingers across the horseshoe so four seams rotate through the air each turn.
example_en: Show me your four-seam grip.
example_es: Enséñame tu agarre de cuatro costuras.

meaning: Index and middle fingers along or near the narrow seams; usually gives more run and sink than a four-seamer.
example_en: Try the two-seam grip on this one.
example_es: Prueba el agarre de dos costuras en este.

meaning: How firmly the ball is held and which finger leads pressure; it changes spin direction and feel.
example_en: Less pressure with the index finger.
example_es: Menos presión con el índice.

meaning: Ball held further back in the hand ('choked'); Driveline notes some pitchers do this on changeups to lessen spin and velocity, while others hold the changeup in the fingertips.
example_en: Hold it deeper in your hand.
example_es: Agárrala más adentro en la mano.

meaning: Where the thumb sits: Driveline logs it as 0/25/50 and as flat or tucked. Under the ball may help 'stay through' it; to the side may help 'get around' it.
example_en: Where do you put your thumb?
example_es: ¿Dónde pones el pulgar?

meaning: Forearm turning thumb-down/palm-out through release; associated with changeups and two-seamers.
example_en: Let your hand turn over naturally.
example_es: Deja que la mano se voltee natural.
region_note: 'Pronación' is technical; with players describe the motion. 'Virar' is common Caribbean for 'turn'.

meaning: To test small grip changes and see (and measure) how the pitch changes.
example_en: Let's experiment with this grip for five throws.
example_es: Vamos a probar este agarre por cinco tiros.

meaning: The pitcher's primary, hardest pitch.
example_en: Throw me three fastballs.
example_es: Tírame tres rectas.
region_note: Diario Libre uses both 'recta' (also 'rectazo' for a hard one) and 'bola rápida' (read in full). 'La rápida' alone was not found in any page read; confirm with a Dominican coach.

meaning: Fastball thrown with the four-seam grip, usually with high backspin and carry.
example_en: Your four-seamer had good carry today.
example_es: Tu recta de cuatro costuras tuvo buen carry hoy.

meaning: Fastball with the two-seam grip; typically more arm-side run and sink.
example_en: The two-seamer is running well.
example_es: La de dos se está moviendo bien.

meaning: Fastball designed to sink and run to the arm side; often overlaps with the two-seamer.
example_en: Keep the sinker down.
example_es: Mantén el sinker abajo.
region_note: MLB.com en español writes 'el sinker' (masculine) and 'sinker de dos costuras'; ESPN Deportes once wrote 'una sinker'. Teach the masculine.

meaning: Fastball with a slightly off-centre grip that moves a little to the glove side.
example_en: Your cutter is cutting too much.
example_es: Tu cutter está cortando demasiado.
region_note: 'Recta cortada' appears in MLB.com en español (Alcántara's repertoire, separate from the slider); Diario Libre wrote 'recta cortante'. 'Cutter' is the field word.

meaning: Breaking ball thrown harder than a curve, with lateral break and often gyro spin.
example_en: Your slider is spinning like a bullet, good.
example_es: Tu slider está girando como una bala, bien.
region_note: 'El slider' (masculine) in Diario Libre and MLB.com en español. 'Deslizador' is a literal translation rarely heard on the field.

meaning: Slider with large horizontal (sweeping) break.
example_en: This one looked more like a sweeper.
example_es: Este pareció más un sweeper.
region_note: MLB.com en español also says 'slider tipo sweeper'.

meaning: Breaking ball with topspin that breaks downward.
example_en: Get on top of the curveball.
example_es: Ponte encima de la curva.

meaning: Off-speed pitch that looks like the fastball but arrives slower.
example_en: Same arm speed on the changeup.
example_es: La misma velocidad de brazo en el cambio.

meaning: Changeup grip with thumb and index finger forming an 'O' on the side of the ball.
example_en: Make the circle with your thumb and index finger.
example_es: Haz el círculo con el pulgar y el índice.
region_note: MLB.com en español describes the grip ('el pulgar y el dedo índice formando un círculo') but no Spanish name for the pitch was found; 'circle change' and 'cambio de círculo' both plausible. Confirm.

meaning: Pitch held with index and middle fingers spread wide; low spin and late drop.
example_en: Spread the fingers a little more on the splitter.
example_es: Separa un poquito más los dedos en el splitter.

meaning: Rotation of the ball after release.
example_en: Good spin on that one.
example_es: Buen spin en ese.
region_note: 'Rotación' is the safe technical word; 'efecto' is everyday Spanish for spin on a ball.

meaning: Revolutions per minute at release.
example_en: Your spin rate went up two hundred.
example_es: Te subieron las revoluciones doscientas.
region_note: MLB.com en español uses 'tasa de rotación' and 'RPM'.

meaning: The line the ball spins around; with spin direction it predicts the direction of spin-induced movement.
example_en: The spin axis tilted more than usual.
example_es: El eje de rotación se inclinó más de lo normal.

meaning: Direction of spin read on a clock face; 12:00 is pure backspin, 6:00 pure topspin.
example_en: That fastball was at one o'clock.
example_es: Esa recta estuvo a la una.
region_note: Clock readings ('a la una y media') are natural Spanish; 'tilt' as a loanword is plausible but unverified. Savant shows spin direction from the hitter's perspective by default; say which view you mean.

meaning: Share of total spin that contributes to movement; gyro spin is the rest.
example_en: Your efficiency was low, so it moved less.
example_es: La eficiencia estuvo baja, por eso se movió menos.
region_note: No Spanish source found for a standard term.

meaning: Spin around the direction of travel (like a bullet or football spiral); adds little movement.
example_en: That slider has a lot of gyro.
example_es: Ese slider tiene mucho gyro.
region_note: Comparing it to 'una bala' is a useful plain explanation.

meaning: Research concept: seams can make the air leave one side of the ball differently, creating an asymmetric wake and a force separate from spin (Magnus); most studied on sinkers.
example_en: The seams are giving you extra sink.
example_es: Las costuras te están dando más caída.
region_note: No Spanish source found; in player talk describe the effect ('las costuras') rather than naming it. Not a coaching cue.

meaning: How far and in what direction the pitch deviates from a straight path.
example_en: Good movement on that one.
example_es: Buen movimiento en ese.

meaning: Movement of a breaking ball or the amount a pitch moves.
example_en: The slider had a late break.
example_es: El slider tuvo un quiebre tarde.

meaning: Downward movement, more than a normal fastball's.
example_en: The changeup dropped at the end.
example_es: El cambio se cayó al final.

es_alt: se mueve hacia tu lado del brazo
meaning: Horizontal movement toward the pitcher's throwing-arm side.
example_en: Your sinker ran more today.
example_es: Tu sinker corrió más hoy.
region_note: 'Correr' for run is the natural verb; 'la corrida' as a noun is unverified.

meaning: A fastball that drops less than the hitter expects because of backspin (high induced vertical break).
example_en: That fastball had good carry.
example_es: Esa recta tuvo buen carry.
region_note: 'Ride' appears in MLB.com en español; avoid literal 'llevar' or 'montar'.

meaning: Vertical movement caused by spin with gravity removed; positive means 'rise', negative extra drop.
example_en: Your IVB was seventeen inches.
example_es: Tu movimiento vertical fue de diecisiete pulgadas.
region_note: Spanish term is descriptive; 'IVB' (i-ve-be) is likely in data talk.

meaning: Side-to-side movement caused by spin, in inches.
example_en: More horizontal break than last week.
example_es: Más movimiento horizontal que la semana pasada.

meaning: Difference in velocity and movement between two pitches.
example_en: We want more separation between the fastball and the changeup.
example_es: Queremos más diferencia entre la recta y el cambio.

meaning: Pitch speed, usually in miles per hour in the DR.
example_en: You were at ninety-four today.
example_es: Estuviste en noventa y cuatro millas hoy.

meaning: The full pitching motion from setup to follow-through.
example_en: Your mechanics looked smooth.
example_es: La mecánica se vio suave.

meaning: Control of the body over the back leg before moving to the plate.
example_en: Stay balanced at the top.
example_es: Mantén el balance arriba.
region_note: 'Balance' is common Caribbean Spanish for this; 'equilibrio' is standard.

meaning: Position of the trunk and head through the delivery.
example_en: Keep your posture tall.
example_es: Mantén la postura alta.

meaning: Raising the stride leg at the start of the delivery.
example_en: A little higher leg lift.
example_es: Levanta la pierna un poquito más.

meaning: Step toward the plate with the lead leg; includes direction and length.
example_en: Your stride was a little short.
example_es: El paso te quedó un poquito corto.
region_note: 'Zancada' is correct but formal; 'el paso' is more natural in field talk (unverified).

en: stride direction / line to the plate
meaning: Where the lead foot lands relative to the line to the plate (closed, on line, open).
example_en: Your foot landed closed. Aim it at the catcher.
example_es: El pie te cayó cerrado. Apúntalo al cátcher.

meaning: Pelvis; begins rotation toward the plate before the trunk.
example_en: Let your hips lead.
example_es: Deja que las caderas vayan primero.

meaning: Trunk and shoulder line; rotates after the hips.
example_en: Keep your shoulders closed a little longer.
example_es: Mantén los hombros cerrados un poquito más.

es: la separación de cadera y hombros
meaning: Angle between the pelvis and the shoulders around foot strike; individual, no single correct value.
example_en: Your separation looked better today.
example_es: La separación se vio mejor hoy.

meaning: Throwing arm; 'tener brazo' means to throw hard.
example_en: How does your arm feel today?
example_es: ¿Cómo sientes el brazo hoy?

meaning: Route of the throwing arm from hand break to release.
example_en: Your arm path looks shorter.
example_es: El recorrido del brazo se ve más corto.

meaning: Angle of the arm at release; Statcast scale 0 degrees (sidearm) to 90 degrees (over the top).
example_en: Keep the same arm angle on the changeup.
example_es: Mantén el mismo ángulo del brazo en el cambio.

meaning: Where in space the ball leaves the hand.
example_en: Your release point was more consistent.
example_es: El punto de salida estuvo más consistente.
region_note: Which Spanish term is standard was not verified; 'donde sueltas la pelota' is safest with players.

meaning: How far in front of the rubber the ball is released, in feet; more extension raises perceived velocity.
example_en: You got more extension today.
example_es: Hoy tuviste más extensión.

meaning: Stride leg, which lands and firms up.
example_en: Firm up your front leg.
example_es: Afirma la pierna delantera.
region_note: 'Alante' is common Caribbean colloquial for 'adelante'.

meaning: Deceleration of arm and body after release.
example_en: Finish your pitch.
example_es: Termina el lanzamiento.

meaning: Speed and rhythm of the delivery.
example_en: Good tempo, keep it.
example_es: Buen ritmo, mantenlo.

meaning: Order and timing of body segments (hips, trunk, arm, hand).
example_en: Your timing was off on that one.
example_es: El timing se te fue en ese.
region_note: Loanword status inferred, not verified.

meaning: Doing the same delivery and release pitch after pitch.
example_en: We want you to repeat this delivery.
example_es: Queremos que repitas esta mecánica.

meaning: Practice area for warming up, and the relief staff; also a practice session.
example_en: Go to the bullpen.
example_es: Ve al bullpen.

meaning: Planned practice throwing session off a mound.
example_en: Tomorrow you have a bullpen session.
example_es: Mañana tienes sesión de bullpen.
region_note: MLB.com en español writes both 'sesión del bullpen' and 'sesiones de bullpen'.

meaning: Number of pitches thrown; basis of workload limits.
example_en: Twenty-five pitches today.
example_es: Veinticinco lanzamientos hoy.

meaning: Open question asking the pitcher for his own sensation first.
example_en: How did that one feel?
example_es: ¿Cómo se sintió ese?

meaning: Request for one more pitch.
example_en: One more just like that.
example_es: Uno más igualito.

meaning: Request to repeat.
example_en: Again, same grip.
example_es: Otra vez, el mismo agarre.

meaning: Short positive feedback.
example_en: Good pitch! That's it.
example_es: ¡Buen lanzamiento! Así mismo.

meaning: Invitation to review high-speed or bullpen video together.
example_en: Let's watch the video together.
example_es: Vamos a ver el video juntos.

meaning: Checking whether a change feels comfortable and repeatable before adopting it.
example_en: Does this grip feel natural to you?
example_es: ¿Este agarre se te siente natural?

es_alt: en lo que te vas a enfocar
meaning: One goal for a group of throws.
example_en: These five, focus only on the location.
example_es: En estos cinco, enfócate solo en la localización.

meaning: Ability to throw strikes (control) and to hit specific spots (command).
example_en: Today we're working on command.
example_es: Hoy vamos a trabajar el control.
region_note: 'Comando' is used for command in Caribbean baseball (search hits); verify the distinction players make.

meaning: Command for placing a finger or the ball.
example_en: Put your finger here.
example_es: Pon el dedo aquí.

meaning: Command for shifting a finger or the ball slightly.
example_en: Move your thumb a little.
example_es: Mueve el pulgar un poquito.

meaning: Command to spread fingers apart.
example_en: Spread your fingers a little more.
example_es: Separa los dedos un poquito más.

meaning: Command to bring fingers closer.
example_en: Bring your fingers together.
example_es: Junta los dedos.

meaning: Command to reduce grip pressure.
example_en: Loosen your grip.
example_es: Afloja el agarre.

meaning: Command to increase pressure.
example_en: Squeeze a little more with the middle finger.
example_es: Aprieta un poquito más con el dedo del medio.

meaning: Command about letting the ball go; also 'soltar' for release in general.
example_en: Let it go out front.
example_es: Suéltala alante.

meaning: Command to maintain a position or feeling.
example_en: Keep that feeling.
example_es: Mantén esa sensación.
region_note: Use 'sensación', not 'sentimiento' (emotion).

meaning: Command to test something new.
example_en: Try this grip.
example_es: Prueba este agarre.

meaning: Command to do the same again.
example_en: Repeat that one.
example_es: Repite ese.

meaning: Player who pitches.
example_en: Pitchers, to the bullpen.
example_es: Píchers, al bullpen.
region_note: Spelled without 't' per RAE/Fundéu; 'serpentinero' is press language.

meaning: To throw the ball to the batter; 'tirar' is the everyday verb.
example_en: Throw me a changeup.
example_es: Tírame un cambio.
region_note: 'Pichar' has non-baseball colloquial meanings in the DR (ignoring someone); 'tirar'/'lanzar' are safer.

meaning: One delivered ball; also a pitch type.
example_en: That pitch was perfect.
example_es: Ese lanzamiento fue perfecto.
region_note: Dominican press writes 'picheo'; MLB.com en español 'pitcheo'.

meaning: Raised dirt area from which the pitcher throws.
example_en: Get on the mound.
example_es: Sube al montículo.
region_note: 'Subir al montículo' confirmed in Diario Libre; columnists also write 'la colina'. DLE lists 'lomita' for Cuba, Nicaragua, Puerto Rico and Venezuela. 'La loma' for the DR is often cited but was not found in any page read.

meaning: Five-sided plate the pitcher throws over.
example_en: Finish toward the plate.
example_es: Termina hacia el plato.

meaning: Area over the plate where a pitch is a strike.
example_en: Attack the zone.
example_es: Ataca la zona.

meaning: Pitch in the zone or swung at and missed.
example_en: First-pitch strike.
example_es: Strike en el primer lanzamiento.

meaning: Pitch outside the zone not swung at.
example_en: That was a ball, but close.
example_es: Esa fue bola, pero cerca.
region_note: Distinct from 'la pelota' (the object).

meaning: Out on three strikes.
example_en: Two strikeouts in the inning.
example_es: Dos ponches en el inning.
region_note: 'Estás ponchao' colloquially means 'you're in trouble'.

meaning: Player who receives the pitch.
example_en: Look at the catcher's glove.
example_es: Mira el guante del cátcher.

meaning: Coach responsible for pitchers.
example_en: I'm your pitching coach this season.
example_es: Soy tu coach de pitcheo esta temporada.

meaning: Official who calls balls and strikes.
example_en: The umpire is calling the low pitch.
example_es: El ampaya está cantando el bajito.
region_note: 'Ampaya' is the DR and Cuba form.

meaning: Ball-flight data from tracking devices.
example_en: Let's look at the numbers.
example_es: Vamos a ver los números.
region_note: 'La data' is a common Spanglish form in baseball; verify.

meaning: Total amount of throwing over a period; guides limits and rest.
example_en: We're watching your workload.
example_es: Estamos cuidando tu carga de trabajo.

meaning: Discomfort the pitcher must report; any pain stops a session and goes to medical staff.
example_en: Does anything hurt?
example_es: ¿Te duele algo?
region_note: Ask both: '¿Te duele?' (pain) and '¿Te molesta?' (discomfort).
